text:
Marcus Pettersson does one thing in New York and it is the job the Rangers need done: take chances away. He has played about 21 minutes a night in all 20 games, with 30 blocked shots and 4 assists, and has not scored. He has 12 shots and 0.62 expected goals all season; nobody expects otherwise.

The defensive case comes mostly from last season in Vancouver. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.23 fewer expected goals per 60 with him on the ice (98th percentile among defensemen), even with weak teammates around him, along with very little offense. This season the Rangers have had 50% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, a bit below their rate without him, so the early read is ordinary rather than elite.

He is not quick (his top speed is in the bottom tenth of the league on NHL EDGE) and he will not move the puck up ice much. What to watch is whether his pairing's chances against stay down as the minutes keep coming.
headline: Marcus Pettersson is the Rangers' stay-at-home partner
